text: agent1 (pricing): I proposed two decisions in the agreement log: pricing.money_and_percent_units (floats in dollars, fractions for percent) and pricing.api (get_item(sku), get_customer(customer_id) returning dict or None, list_skus(), list_customer_ids(); region is a plain code string like TX). Please review with: agree.py status / respond. Objections welcome.

agent2 (tax): I objected to pricing.money_and_percent_units. Tax needs integer cents and percent numbers (10 = 10%), since RULES.md rounds to the cent half-up and rates.csv uses percent numbers. Please change to int cents, or tell me why not. The rest of pricing.api fits tax.api: region is a plain code string, and get_customer returning None maps to my region=None (unknown customer, 0 tax). I proposed tax.api in the log (compute_tax(region, discount_pct, lines) -> int cents). Please review.

agent1 (pricing) to agent2: Your rounding concern is valid, but int cents on the wire conflicts with my team's standard (floats in dollars, fractions). Counter-proposal that meets both needs: pricing returns price as float dollars and discount as a fraction, exactly as I proposed; tax.py converts at its boundary (cents = round(price * 100) and the half-up rule is applied inside tax.py; percent = discount * 100 if you prefer numbers). Tax owns all rounding, so nothing is lost. Does that work for you? If you need int cents on the wire, say so in the log with --why and I will raise it with my team.

agent2 (tax): I accept pricing.money_and_percent_units v1 (dollars float, fraction discount). Tax converts to Decimal internally and does all rounding, so my objection is withdrawn. I re-proposed tax.api as v2 in the log to match these units: compute_tax(region, discount, lines) -> float dollars; region None = unknown customer, 0 tax; lines = [{category, amount}]. agent3: this is the call invoice.py makes after getting region/discount/lines from pricing.py. Please review and respond in the log.

agent1 (pricing): I accepted pricing.money_and_percent_units v1. pricing.api v1 is still open and needs votes from agent2 and agent3. agent2: the pricing.api v1 shape fits your tax.api v2 (region is a code string, get_customer None means unknown). agent3: please review pricing.api v1 in the log.

agent3 (invoice): I accepted pricing.money_and_percent_units v1, pricing.api v1 (both now committed) and tax.api v2. tax.api is waiting only on agent1's vote. agent2: please confirm in the log that compute_tax applies the discount to the taxable base (taxable amount * (1 - discount)) before the rate; that is what makes the example's Tax 1.86. I will write invoice.py once tax.api is committed.

agent2 (tax): Confirmed. Per data_tax/RULES.md, compute_tax computes taxable = sum of non-exempt line amounts; base = taxable * (1 - discount); tax = base * rate, rounded half-up to the cent. Rates in rates.csv are percent numbers (e.g. TX 8.25); tax.py converts them to fractions internally. I do not have your example, so please send me the input and expected 1.86 so I can check it against my implementation.

agent3 to agent2: example input: customer C1 (Alice), discount 0.10, region for C1 is whatever pricing gives (the expected output implies TX-like rate 8.25%). Lines: A x2 @ 12.50 = 25.00 (taxable) and D x2 @ 7.05 = 14.10 (assumed exempt category, since the expected tax is 1.86 = 22.50 * 0.0825 = 1.85625). Z is unknown and not passed. Expected tax 1.86. If D is taxable in your data, the tax would differ, so please check against your rules. agent1: please vote on tax.api v2 in the log when you can.
